messages.author: e5411f2948e070c1
messages.subject: Legend.key blacked out
parts:
ggplot2 is a nice system, though sometimes a bit of a struggle for
this new R user ;-) I have two questions which the code example
illustrates using ggplot2 sample datasets. For now, qplot seems to
provide all I need without going to ggplot. When layering 2 datasets
on the same plot the legends were initially tangled up, but the
documentation's suggestion of specifying "labels=" and "breaks=" in
"scale_xxx_manual" straightened that out.

Question 1: plot p below has my "rates" legend just as I want it. When
I add the rectangle shading layer from another dataset in plot pb, the
first, "rates" legend.key gets blacked out--though the second, new
legend is perfect. I suspect the legend.key problem is related to
ggplot's combining info from the line & rect geoms for a default
legend.key. Specifying labels= and breaks= cleared up some similar
interference between layers, but how might I keep the black shading
out of the geom="line" legend? I tried changing some legend.key theme
settings, but couldn't figure out anything which worked.

Question 2: the example also illustrates a minor question (which I can
fix mechanically, but I'm curious about). Note that the "party" data
in df. presidential are "Republican" & "Democratic" and the first
rectangle on plot pb is blue, even though I specified colors as "red",
"blue" in that order. I can correct this and get red mapped to
Republican by specifying the colors in reverse order. I haven't found
it mentioned, but suspect this behavior is because ggplot2 maps the
color list to the variable=party elements in "alphabetic or ascii sort
order." Is this correct?

Many thanks to Hadley for providing this great tool!

#plotecon.r example
economicsw <- melt(economics, measure=c("psavert", "uempmed"),
id="date")

p <- qplot(date, value, data=economicsw, geom="line")
p <- p + aes(colour=variable) +
scale_colour_manual(name="rates", c("black", "chartreuse3"),
labels=c("personal savings", "unemployment"), breaks=c("psavert",
"uempmed"))
p <- p + opts(title = "economics info")
p <- p + ylab("saving, unemp rates")
print(p)

y_max <- max(c(economics$psavert), max(economics$uempmed))
y_min <- min(c(economics$psavert), max(economics$uempmed))
yrng <- c(y_min, y_max)

presidential$variable <- presidential$party

pb <- p + geom_rect(aes( xmin = start, xmax = end, y = NULL, x = NULL,
fill = party), ymin = yrng[1], ymax = yrng[2], data=presidential) +
scale_fill_manual(name="critter", values = alpha(c("red", "blue"),
0.2),
labels = c("elephant", "donkey") )#, breaks=c("Republican",
"Democratic") )
print(pb)

Hmmm, that's weird. I think it might be a bug. Would you mind trying
to create a mimimal example that illustrates the problem?

> Question 2: the example also illustrates a minor question (which I can
> fix mechanically, but I'm curious about). Note that the "party" data
> in df. presidential are "Republican" & "Democratic" and the first
> rectangle on plot pb is blue, even though I specified colors as "red",
> "blue" in that order. I can correct this and get red mapped to

> it mentioned, but suspect this behavior is because ggplot2 maps the
> color list to the variable=party elements in "alphabetic or ascii sort

Yes - ggplot2 uses the ordering of the underlying factor, which is
alphabetic by default.
